questions.question: A car travels 209 km in the first hour and 83 km in the second hour. What is the average speed (in km/hr) of the car for the whole journey?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

When the travel time for different segments of a journey is identical, the average speed is the direct arithmetic mean of the speeds.

Speed in the 1st hour = 209 km/hr

Speed in the 2nd hour = 83 km/hr

Average speed = (209 + 83) ÷ 2 = 292 ÷ 2 = 146 km/hr.

**∴ The correct answer is 146 km/hr.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Distance covered in the first hour (D₁) = 209 km

Distance covered in the second hour (D₂) = 83 km

Time taken for the first distance (T₁) = 1 hour

Time taken for the second distance (T₂) = 1 hour

**Formula Used:**

Average Speed = Total Distance ÷ Total Time

 
• 
 D₁ = 209 km 
 D₂ = 83 km T₁ = 1 hr T₂ = 1 hr Total Distance = 292 km | Total Time = 2 hrs 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Total Distance = 209 + 83

⇒ Total Distance = 292 km

⇒ Total Time = 1 + 1

⇒ Total Time = 2 hours

⇒ Average Speed = 292 ÷ 2

⇒ Average Speed = 146 km/hr

**∴ The correct answer is 146 km/hr.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Average Speed (Equal Distances)

When a car covers two equal distances at varying speeds of x and y, the formula for average speed directly becomes 2xy ÷ (x + y).

Average Speed (Equal Time Intervals)

If a vehicle travels at different speeds S₁, S₂, ... Sₙ for strictly equal time intervals, the overall average speed is perfectly equal to their arithmetic mean: (S₁ + S₂ + ... + Sₙ) ÷ n.

Relative Speed

For two moving bodies, if they travel in the same direction, their relative speed is computed as the difference of their individual speeds (S₁ − S₂). If travelling in opposite directions, it is the sum of their individual speeds (S₁ + S₂).

questions.question: Pipe A can fill a tank in 6 minutes, while pipe B can empty the completely filled tank in 12 minutes. Initially, pipe A is opened and after 2 minutes pipe B is also opened. In how much time (in minutes) will the remaining tank be filled completely?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Total capacity = LCM of 6 and 12 = 12 units.

Efficiency of filling Pipe A = +2 units/min | Efficiency of emptying Pipe B = −1 unit/min.

Work completed by A in first 2 mins = 2 × 2 = 4 units.

Remaining work = 12 − 4 = 8 units.

Time for (A + B) to complete the remaining work = 8 ÷ (2 − 1) = 8 minutes.

**∴ The correct answer is 8 minutes.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

questions.question: An article is marked at ₹2,000. A shopkeeper offers a discount of 25% on the article. What is the selling price of the article after the discount?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

A 25% discount means the Selling Price is 75% of the Marked Price.

Fraction value of 75% = 3/4

SP = 3/4 × ₹2000

SP = 3 × ₹500 = ₹1500

**∴ The correct answer is ₹1500.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Marked Price (MP) = ₹2000

Discount = 25%

**Formula Used:**

Selling Price (SP) = MP − Discount

Discount = MP × (Discount % ÷ 100)

 
 
 

 
 
 
 
 
 MP = ₹2000
 (100%)
 
 
 
• 
 − 25% Discount
 (− ₹500)
 
 
 
 SP = ₹1500
 (75%)

**Calculations:**

⇒ Discount amount = 2000 × (25 ÷ 100)

⇒ Discount amount = 2000 × (1 ÷ 4) = ₹500

⇒ Selling Price = 2000 − 500 = ₹1500

**∴ The correct answer is ₹1500.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Marked Price & Discount

Discount is an allowance given to the buyer and is always calculated on the Marked Price (MP) or List Price of an article.

Successive Discount

If two successive discounts of A% and B% are given, the equivalent single discount percentage is calculated as: A + B − (A × B ÷ 100).

Profit and Loss Calculation

While Discount is applied to the Marked Price, Profit or Loss percentage is always calculated on the original Cost Price (CP) of the item.

questions.question: Poonam, Qasim and Rina invest ₹1,92,000, ₹1,20,000, and ₹88,000, respectively to start a business. If the profit at the end of the year is ₹4,93,600, then what is the share of Rina in the profit?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Profit ratio = Investment ratio (since the time period is the same for all)

Poonam : Qasim : Rina = 192000 : 120000 : 88000 = 192 : 120 : 88 = 24 : 15 : 11

Total profit parts = 24 + 15 + 11 = 50 parts

50 parts = ₹4,93,600 ⇒ 1 part = ₹9,872

Rina's share = 11 parts = 11 × 9,872 = ₹1,08,592

**∴ The correct answer is ₹1,08,592.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Poonam's investment = ₹1,92,000

Qasim's investment = ₹1,20,000

Rina's investment = ₹88,000

Total profit at the end of the year = ₹4,93,600

**Formula Used:**

Profit ratio = (Capital₁ × Time₁) : (Capital₂ × Time₂) : (Capital₃ × Time₃)

 
 Poonam
 ₹192k
 24 parts
 
 
 Qasim
 ₹120k
 15 parts

 
 Rina
 ₹88k
 11 parts

 
 Total Profit: ₹4,93,600 (50 parts)

**Calculations:**

⇒ Since the time period is exactly one year for all three partners, the profit will be distributed directly in proportion to their respective investments.

⇒ Profit Ratio = 1,92,000 : 1,20,000 : 88,000

⇒ Cancelling three zeros from each term gives:

⇒ Profit Ratio = 192 : 120 : 88

⇒ Dividing by the common factor 8:

⇒ Profit Ratio = 24 : 15 : 11

⇒ Sum of the ratio parts = 24 + 15 + 11 = 50 parts

⇒ Total profit corresponding to 50 parts = ₹4,93,600

⇒ Value of 1 part = 4,93,600 ÷ 50 = ₹9,872

⇒ Share of Rina in the profit = 11 parts × 9,872

⇒ Rina's share = ₹1,08,592

**∴ The correct answer is ₹1,08,592.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Simple Partnership

When the investments of all the partners are for the same time period, the profits are distributed directly in the ratio of their invested capitals.

Compound Partnership

When the investments are for different time periods, the profit ratio is calculated as the product of capital and time: P₁ : P₂ = (C₁ × T₁) : (C₂ × T₂).

Working vs Sleeping Partner

A working partner actively manages the business and often receives a fixed percentage of profit as salary before the remaining profit is distributed among all partners based on their capital.

questions.question: A packaging company requires cardboard for two sizes of rectangular boxes. The larger box measures 30 cm × 25 cm × 10 cm, and the smaller one measures 18 cm × 12 cm × 10 cm. An additional 6% of the total surface area is needed for overlaps. If cardboard costs ₹45 per 10,000 cm², calculate the total cost (in ₹, rounded off to the nearest hundreds) of cardboard needed to produce 400 big boxes and 500 small boxes.
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

TSA (big box) = 2(lb + bh + hl) = 2(750 + 250 + 300) = 2600 cm²

Total for 400 = 2600 × 400 = 10,40,000 cm²

TSA (small box) = 2(216 + 120 + 180) = 1032 cm²

Total for 500 = 1032 × 500 = 5,16,000 cm²

Total area = 15,56,000 cm²

Add 6% → 15,56,000 × 1.06 = 16,49,360 cm²

Cost = (16,49,360 / 10,000) × 45 ≈ 7422.12

**∴ Answer = ₹7,400 (approx)**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Big box: 30×25×10, Small box: 18×12×10

Cost = ₹45 per 10,000 cm², extra = 6%

**Formula used:**

TSA = 2(lb + bh + hl)

**Calculation:**

⇒ Big box TSA = 2(750 + 250 + 300) = 2600

⇒ 400 boxes → 2600 × 400 = 10,40,000

⇒ Small box TSA = 2(216 + 120 + 180) = 1032

⇒ 500 boxes → 1032 × 500 = 5,16,000

⇒ Total = 15,56,000 cm²

⇒ Including 6% = 15,56,000 × 1.06 = 16,49,360 cm²

⇒ Cost = (16,49,360 ÷ 10,000) × 45 ≈ 7422.12

⇒ Rounded to nearest hundred = 7400

**∴ The total cost is ₹7,400.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Surface Area

TSA = 2(lb + bh + hl)

Bulk Calculation

Multiply TSA by number of boxes.

Extra Allowance

Add percentage increase for overlaps.

Cost Conversion

Divide by 10,000 before multiplying cost.

questions.question: Walking at (5)/(6) of his normal speed from his home, Tarun is 16 minutes late in reaching his office. The usual time taken by him to cover the distance between his home and his office is:
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Speed = 5/6 → Time = 6/5 (inverse)

Increase in time = (6/5 − 1) = 1/5 of usual time

Given increase = 16 minutes

So (1/5) time = 16 → time = 80 minutes

**∴ Answer = 80 minutes**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Reduced speed = (5/6) of normal speed, delay = 16 minutes

**Formula used:**

Time = Distance ÷ Speed

**Calculation:**

⇒ Let usual time = t minutes

⇒ New time = (6/5)t

⇒ Increase = (6/5)t − t = (1/5)t

⇒ (1/5)t = 16

⇒ t = 80

**∴ The usual time is 80 minutes.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Inverse Relation

Speed and time are inversely proportional.

Speed Reduction

If speed = a/b, time = b/a

Time Difference

Extra time = new − original

Shortcut Insight

Use fractional increase directly.

questions.question: The monthly incomes of two friends Chetan and Vipul are in the ratio 5 : 9 respectively and each of them saves ₹45,000 every month. If the ratio of their monthly expenditure is 2 : 4, then find the monthly income of Chetan (in ₹).
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Income ratio = 5 : 9 → incomes = 5x, 9x

Expenditure ratio = 2 : 4 → expenditures = 2y, 4y

Savings = Income − Expenditure = 45000

So 5x − 2y = 45000 and 9x − 4y = 45000

Subtract → 4x − 2y = 0 ⇒ 2x = y

Substitute → 5x − 4x = 45000 ⇒ x = 45000

**∴ Chetan’s income = 5x = ₹2,25,000**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Income ratio = 5 : 9, Expenditure ratio = 2 : 4, Savings = 45000 each

**Formula used:**

Savings = Income − Expenditure

**Calculation:**

⇒ Let incomes = 5x and 9x

⇒ Let expenditures = 2y and 4y

⇒ For Chetan: 5x − 2y = 45000

⇒ For Vipul: 9x − 4y = 45000

⇒ Subtract equations:

⇒ (9x − 4y) − (5x − 2y) = 0

⇒ 4x − 2y = 0 ⇒ y = 2x

⇒ Substitute in first equation:

⇒ 5x − 2(2x) = 45000

⇒ x = 45000

⇒ Chetan’s income = 5x = 225000

**∴ The correct answer is ₹2,25,000.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Income-Expenditure Relation

Savings = Income − Expenditure

Ratio Method

Assume variables for ratios.

Equation Solving

Form simultaneous equations.

Substitution

Use one equation to simplify the other.

questions.question: A father is currently four times as old as his son. Eighteen years from now, the father will be twice as old as his son. What is the father's present age?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Let son’s age = x → father = 4x

After 18 years: 4x + 18 = 2(x + 18)

4x + 18 = 2x + 36 → 2x = 18 → x = 9

**∴ Father’s age = 4x = 36 years**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Father = 4 × son, After 18 years father = 2 × son

**Formula used:**

Form equation using ages

**Calculation:**

⇒ Let son’s age = x

⇒ Father’s age = 4x

⇒ After 18 years: Father = 4x + 18, Son = x + 18

⇒ 4x + 18 = 2(x + 18)

⇒ 4x + 18 = 2x + 36

⇒ 2x = 18 ⇒ x = 9

⇒ Father’s age = 4x = 36

**∴ The father’s present age is 36 years.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Age Relation

Future Age

questions.question: What is the smallest value of a in the number a3724, so that the number formed is divisible by 3?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Sum of digits = a + 3 + 7 + 2 + 4 = a + 16

For divisibility by 3 → (a + 16) must be multiple of 3

16 ≡ 1 (mod 3) → a + 1 ≡ 0 (mod 3)

a ≡ 2 (mod 3)

Smallest such digit = 2

**∴ Answer = 2**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Number = a3724

**Formula used:**

Divisibility rule of 3 → sum of digits divisible by 3

**Calculation:**

⇒ Sum = a + 3 + 7 + 2 + 4 = a + 16

⇒ For divisibility → (a + 16) divisible by 3

⇒ Try smallest digit values:

⇒ a = 2 → sum = 18 (divisible by 3)

**∴ The smallest value of a is 2.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Trial Method

Check smallest possible digit.

Digit Range

a can be from 0 to 9.

questions.question: The cost of a washing machine is 26% less than the cost of a TV. If the cost of the washing machine increases by 86% and that of the TV decreases by 38%, then what is the percentage change in the total cost of 8 washing machines and 4 TVs?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Let TV = 100 → Washing machine = 74

New WM = 74 × 1.86 = 137.64

New TV = 100 × 0.62 = 62

Initial total = 8×74 + 4×100 = 592 + 400 = 992

New total = 8×137.64 + 4×62 = 1101.12 + 248 = 1349.12

% change = [(1349.12 − 992)/992] × 100 ≈ 36%

**∴ Answer = 36% increase**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Washing machine is 26% less than TV

Increase = 86% (WM), Decrease = 38% (TV)

**Formula used:**

New value = Old value × (1 ± % change)

**Calculation:**

⇒ Let TV = 100 ⇒ WM = 74

⇒ New WM = 74 × 1.86 = 137.64

⇒ New TV = 100 × 0.62 = 62

⇒ Initial total = 8×74 + 4×100 = 992

⇒ New total = 8×137.64 + 4×62 = 1349.12

⇒ Increase = 1349.12 − 992 = 357.12

⇒ % change = (357.12 ÷ 992) × 100 ≈ 36%

**∴ The total cost increases by about 36%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Assumption Method

Assume convenient value (like 100) for easy calculation.

Successive Change

Apply percentage changes separately.

Weighted Total

Multiply by quantity before comparing totals.

Final Percentage

(Change ÷ Original) × 100

Mode

The mode is the value that appears most frequently in a data set. A given set of data may have one mode (unimodal), two modes (bimodal), multiple modes, or no mode at all.

Median

The median is the exact middle value when a data set is ordered from least to greatest. If the total number of elements is even, it is the average of the two central values.

Mean

The mean is the mathematical average of a set of numbers, calculated by dividing the total sum of all observations by the number of observations.

Empirical Relationship

For any moderately skewed statistical distribution, the relationship between measures of central tendency is given by: Mode = 3 × Median − 2 × Mean.

questions.question: If the radius of the base of a right circular cylinder is decreased by 28% and its height is increased by 114%, then what is the percentage increase (rounded off to the nearest integer) in its volume?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Volume ∝ r²h

Radius ↓ 28% → r = 0.72r

Height ↑ 114% → h = 2.14h

New volume factor = (0.72)² × 2.14

= 0.5184 × 2.14 ≈ 1.109

Increase = 1.109 − 1 = 0.109 = 10.9%

**∴ Answer ≈ 11% increase**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Radius decreases by 28% and height increases by 114%

**Concept Used:**

Volume of cylinder = πr²h

**Calculation:**

⇒ New radius = 0.72r

⇒ New height = 2.14h

⇒ New volume = π × (0.72r)² × (2.14h)

⇒ = πr²h × (0.72)² × 2.14

⇒ = πr²h × 0.5184 × 2.14

⇒ = πr²h × 1.109

⇒ Increase = (1.109 − 1) × 100

⇒ = 10.9% ≈ 11%

**∴ The percentage increase in volume is 11%**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Volume Relation

Volume of cylinder depends on r² and h.

Percentage Change

Convert percentage into multiplier form (1 ± change).

Successive Change

Apply changes step-by-step on each dimension.

Key Insight

Radius impacts volume more as it is squared.

questions.question: In quadrilateral PQRS, the bisectors of angle R and angle S meet at the point T (inside the quadrilateral) and angle STR = 24^circ . If the ratio of angle P to angle Q is 5 : 7 , then what is the difference between the measures of angle Q and angle P ?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

In any quadrilateral, the angle between the bisectors of two adjacent angles is exactly half the sum of the remaining two angles.

⇒ ∠STR = (∠P + ∠Q) ÷ 2

⇒ ∠P + ∠Q = 24° × 2 = 48°

The ratio of ∠P to ∠Q is given as 5 : 7, making a total of 12 parts.

⇒ 12 parts = 48° ⇒ 1 part = 4°

⇒ Difference = (7 − 5) parts = 2 × 4° = 8°

**∴ The correct answer is 8°.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Bisectors of ∠R and ∠S meet at point T.

∠STR = 24°

Ratio of ∠P : ∠Q = 5 : 7

 
 
• 
• 
 24° P Q R S T 
 
 

**Formula Used:**

Sum of interior angles in a triangle = 180°

Sum of interior angles in a quadrilateral = 360°

**Calculations:**

⇒ In ΔSTR, ∠STR + (∠TSR) + (∠TRS) = 180°

⇒ Since ST and RT are bisectors, ∠TSR = ∠S ÷ 2 and ∠TRS = ∠R ÷ 2.

⇒ 24° + (∠S ÷ 2) + (∠R ÷ 2) = 180°

⇒ (∠S + ∠R) ÷ 2 = 180° − 24° = 156°

⇒ ∠S + ∠R = 312°

⇒ In quadrilateral PQRS, ∠P + ∠Q + ∠R + ∠S = 360°

⇒ ∠P + ∠Q + 312° = 360°

⇒ ∠P + ∠Q = 48°

⇒ Let ∠P = 5x and ∠Q = 7x (Based on ratio 5 : 7)

⇒ 5x + 7x = 48°

⇒ 12x = 48° ⇒ x = 4°

⇒ Difference between the measures = ∠Q − ∠P

⇒ 7x − 5x = 2x

⇒ Difference = 2 × 4° = 8°

**∴ The correct answer is 8°.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Angle Between Bisectors of Adjacent Angles

In any quadrilateral, the angle formed by the intersection of the angle bisectors of two adjacent angles is equal to half the sum of the remaining two angles. Formula: ∠AOB = (∠C + ∠D) ÷ 2.

Angle Between Bisectors of Opposite Angles

The acute angle formed by the intersection of the angle bisectors of two opposite angles in a quadrilateral is equal to half the absolute difference of the other two angles. Formula: ∠AOB = |∠B − ∠D| ÷ 2.

Sum of Angles of a Quadrilateral

The sum of all interior angles of a quadrilateral is always 360°. This principle serves as the foundational step for proving standard geometry shortcuts involving internal angle divisions.

questions.question: A man buys a car for ₹3,00,000, spends ₹30,000 on modifications and sells it at 5% loss. What is the selling price?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Total CP = ₹3,00,000 + ₹30,000 = ₹3,30,000

SP at a 5% loss is equivalent to 95% of the Total CP.

SP = 0.95 × 3,30,000 = ₹3,13,500

**∴ The correct answer is ₹3,13,500.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

 
 Total Cost Price (CP) ₹3,30,000 Selling Price (SP) ? 
 − 5% Loss SP = 95% of Total CP 

**Given:**

Purchase price = ₹3,00,000

Modification cost = ₹30,000

Loss percentage = 5%

**Formula Used:**

Total CP = Purchase price + Overhead expenses

SP = Total CP × (100 − Loss%) ÷ 100

**Calculations:**

⇒ Total CP = 3,00,000 + 30,000 = ₹3,30,000

⇒ SP = 3,30,000 × (100 − 5) ÷ 100

⇒ SP = 3,30,000 × 95 ÷ 100

⇒ SP = 3300 × 95

⇒ SP = ₹3,13,500

**∴ The correct answer is ₹3,13,500.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Overhead Expenses

All extra costs such as transportation, repairs, or modifications are added to the initial purchase price to form the Effective Cost Price (Total CP).

Selling Price Formula (Loss)

When a transaction results in a loss, the final Selling Price is calculated as: SP = Total CP × (100 − Loss%) ÷ 100.

Selling Price Formula (Profit)

Conversely, when there is a profit, the Selling Price is calculated as: SP = Total CP × (100 + Profit%) ÷ 100.

questions.question: If the perimeter of a rectangle is 500 cm and its length is 1.5 times its breadth, then find the area of the rectangle (in cm² ).

Let breadth = b, length = 1.5b

Perimeter = 2(l + b) = 500 ⇒ l + b = 250

1.5b + b = 2.5b = 250 ⇒ b = 100

l = 150

Area = 150 × 100 = 15000 cm²

**∴ Answer = 15000 cm²**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

⇒ l + b = 250

⇒ Let breadth = b, then length = 1.5b

⇒ 1.5b + b = 250

⇒ 2.5b = 250

⇒ b = 100 cm

⇒ l = 1.5 × 100 = 150 cm

⇒ Area = 150 × 100 = 15000 cm²

**∴ The area of the rectangle is 15000 cm²**

questions.question: P and Q together can fill a cistern with water in 6 hours. If P alone can fill the cistern with water in 24 hours, then in how many hours will Q alone fill one-fourth of the same cistern with water?
questions.solution: [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__ Let total capacity of the cistern = LCM of 6 and 24 = 24 units. Efficiency of (P + Q) = 24 ÷ 6 = 4 units/hour. Efficiency of P = 24 ÷ 24 = 1 unit/hour. Efficiency of Q = 4 − 1 = 3 units/hour. Time taken by Q to fill 1/4th of the cistern = (24 × 1/4) ÷ 3 = 6 ÷ 3 = 2 hours. **∴ The correct answer is 2 hours.**
